title: The "where did it go?" audit
description: When money seems to vanish between payday and month's end, a calm look at three months of statements usually finds the leak.

body.heading: Gather the evidence
paragraphs: Open three months of bank statements. You are looking for patterns, not individual embarrassments, so work through them quickly and highlight anything that repeats.

Repeating payments are the interesting ones: subscriptions, regular takeaways on the same weekday, top-ups, delivery fees. One-off spending is life; repeated spending is a system, and systems can be redesigned.

body.heading: Name the top three leaks
paragraphs: Add up each repeated pattern across the three months. A $9 weekly charge is $117 over a quarter; a $15 twice-weekly habit comes to nearly $400. Seeing the quarterly figure changes how a "small" charge feels.
Pick the three largest patterns and ask one question of each: do I still want this, at this frequency, at this price? Often the answer is yes to the thing but no to the frequency.

body.heading: Fix it at the source
paragraphs: Cancel inside the app or account where the payment started, not just by deleting the app. Then check next month's statement to confirm the charge has actually stopped — cancelled subscriptions occasionally keep billing.

Expect the audit to feel uncomfortable for an afternoon and relieving for months. The leaks you find are rarely about willpower; they are about systems set up once and never revisited. Revisiting them is the entire skill.

takeaway: Three months of statements and three honest questions will find where the money goes — and most leaks are repeated small charges, not big ones.
